 Bailey Pemberton Tue, October 27, 2026 at 3:10 AM MDT 4 min read SPOL.OL +2.38% 
 SpareBank 1 Østlandet has delivered a strong share price over recent years, which naturally raises a question for anyone looking at the stock today. Are the returns it earns on its capital enough to justify where the valuation has now moved to? 
 Over the past 3 years the share price is up 97.2%, which makes it important to ask whether the bank's underlying return on capital can sustain that kind of rerating. 
 The business model relies heavily on how efficiently it turns customer deposits and lending into profits, so the level and stability of return on equity and return on invested capital may be crucial for what investors are really paying for. 
 What if you looked at SpareBank 1 Østlandet through its earnings instead? See why SpareBank 1 Østlandet's 11.4x P/E tells a different valuation story . 
 The issue now is whether SpareBank 1 Østlandet's current share price is properly aligned with the returns it earns on the capital entrusted to it. 
 If you want a broader feel for how other businesses are priced on the returns they earn on their capital, it can help to compare SpareBank 1 Østlandet with 195 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Is SpareBank 1 Østlandet a Bargain on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model looks at what SpareBank 1 Østlandet can earn above its cost of equity on each krone of shareholder capital. For this bank, the inputs point to a franchise that clears that hurdle by a reasonable margin. Book Value sits at NOK183.22 per share, with a Stable EPS estimate of NOK19.82 per share based on the median return on equity from the past 5 years, so the framework assumes the bank can keep converting equity into earnings at a similar efficiency level. 
 The cost of equity is put at NOK11.99 per share, while the Excess Return comes out at NOK7.83 per share and the Average Return on Equity is 13.33%. Stable Book Value is modelled at NOK148.65 per share using weighted future estimates from three analysts, which anchors the long term return assumptions. Put together, these inputs produce an Excess Returns valuation that sits substantially above today's NOK199.90 share price, which is why readers often compare this output with.
